name: Logistics and transport
summary: Ethiopia plans to invest over USD 70 billion in transport and logistics infrastructure over the next decade, and the first phase of the Modjo modern logistics hub, with capacity of up to one million 20-foot containers a year, was inaugurated in September 2026. About 95 percent of import-export cargo moves along the Addis-Djibouti corridor and the World Bank estimates logistics costs at nearly a third of GDP, so efficiency gains in truck terminals, dry ports and freight services offer a large opportunity. Ethiopian Airlines carried 897,000 tons of cargo in fiscal year 2025/2026, serving 44 freighter destinations.

opportunities.title: Freight truck terminals
opportunities.detail: The World Bank corridor project will seek to mobilize private sector financing for freight truck terminals, and the national target is to increase cargo vehicle terminals from 1 to 23 by 2030.

opportunities.title: New dry ports and logistics hubs
opportunities.detail: The Ethiopian Investment Commission lists dry ports in Semera, Dire Dawa, Woreta, Mekelle, Kombolcha or Jijiga, a logistics hub at Indode on the Addis-Djibouti railway, and expansion of the Modjo logistics center among opportunities.

opportunities.title: National transport investment pipeline
opportunities.detail: The Commission says it has identified six key investment areas and 29 specific investment opportunities, within a plan to invest over USD 70 billion in transport and logistics infrastructure over the next decade.

opportunities.title: Dire Dawa Free Trade Zone
opportunities.detail: More than 45 large-scale investors are active in the zone, which has handled goods worth over USD 100 million since operations began; IPDC aims to channel nearly 4 billion dollars' worth of goods through it over five years.

opportunities.title: Faster dry port clearance
opportunities.detail: The World Bank reports that, after the World Bank-supported expansion of Modjo Dry Port, processing times have in some cases fallen by 70%, from 60 days to 15.

opportunities.title: Air cargo connectivity
opportunities.detail: Ethiopian Airlines serves 44 freighter destinations alongside 127 international passenger destinations, according to the Ethiopian Investment Commission.

incentives.detail: The Ethiopian Investment Board decision of September 2018 allows joint ventures with international logistics service providers holding up to 49% stakes, including in bonded warehouse, consolidation and deconsolidation services (later 2026 reports of full opening of freight forwarding could not be confirmed in a permitted source).
The Ethiopian Investment Commission states that the 2020 investment law opened many investment areas to FDI, including transport and logistics.
The Ethiopian Maritime Authority said the Dire Dawa Free Trade Zone would provide foreign currency, easy customs and improved logistics services.

risks.detail: Dwell times for trucks and goods at the Djibouti port and the Modjo inland dry port are a cost factor, according to the World Bank; its Addis-Djibouti corridor project is designed to improve corridor efficiency, including through private investment in freight truck terminals.

Road carries most corridor freight and the World Bank expects it to keep doing so even if rail traffic grows to 4 million tons, so trucking, terminals and road-based services remain central to the market.

Project timelines matter for planning: at the October 2024 World Bank mission, 3.3 percent of the US$730 million corridor grant had been disbursed and civil works on the road component had not yet started.

Imported fuel prices are a key operating cost; the IMF noted temporary fuel shortages and sharp fuel price increases in 2026 linked to disruptions in global trade, and that pressures could increase if the disruption is prolonged.
